definitions.explanation: Relating to translation or reference from English to Japanese, especially for dictionaries.

examples.japanese: {英和|えいわ}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
{英和|えいわ}⟦{翻訳|ほんやく}→翻訳：01725_honyaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦アルバイト→アルバイト：01528_arubaito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I have a part-time job doing English-Japanese translation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大|おお}きい→大きい：00335_ookii⟧{英和|えいわ}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{欲|ほ}しい→欲しい：01107_hoshii⟧。
examples.english: I want a big English-Japanese dictionary.

notes:
{英和|えいわ} combines ⟦{英|えい}→英：noentry⟧ (English) and ⟦{和|わ}→和：00418_wa⟧ (Japanese) to indicate the direction from English to Japanese. Almost always used as a modifier before another noun.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {英和|えいわ}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧/⟦{辞書|じしょ}→辞書：04707_jisho⟧ (English-Japanese dictionary)
- {英和|えいわ}⟦{翻訳|ほんやく}→翻訳：01725_honyaku⟧ (English-to-Japanese translation)

DICTIONARY NAMING PATTERN:
Japanese dictionary names follow the pattern {Language A}{Language B} = A-to-B direction:
- {英和|えいわ}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: English → Japanese
- ⟦{和英|わえい}→和英：05253_waei⟧⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: Japanese → English
- ⟦{漢和|かんわ}→漢和：04019_kanwa⟧⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: kanji → Japanese
- ⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: Japanese → Japanese (monolingual)
- ⟦{仏和|ふつわ}→仏和：noentry⟧⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: French → Japanese

USAGE:
⟦{和|わ}→和：00418_wa⟧ in this context means "Japanese" (from ⟦{大和|やまと}→大和：12261_yamato⟧). It appears in many language-pair terms.
